benefit.name: BC Disability Assistance (PWD)
benefit.amount: Up to $1,483.50/month single ($983.50 support + $500 shelter) plus $52/month transportation supplement; up to $2,662/month for a couple where both have PWD
benefit.summary: Monthly income support for adults with the Persons with Disabilities (PWD) designation — a support allowance plus shelter allowance, an automatic $52 transportation supplement, health supplements and PharmaCare Plan C coverage.
benefit.note: Rates took effect December 1, 2025. As of July 2026, $1,483.50 for a single person is the current maximum. You can also work. Starting January 1, 2026, you can earn up to $16,200 a year before earnings change your payment. The limit is $23,400 for a couple where one of you has PWD and $32,400 where both do. There is no monthly cap, so you can earn it whenever suits you. Even if you go over the limit, you always keep 100% of the money you earn. Only the assistance payment is reduced.

detail.about: Disability assistance is BC's core income program for people with the PWD designation. A single person receives a $983.50 monthly support allowance plus a shelter allowance of up to $500 (for one person the minimum is $75 if your actual shelter costs are less), and every PWD recipient gets a $52 transportation supplement as cash or an in-kind bus pass. It also opens the door to dental, optical, medical equipment, medical transportation and nutrition supplements, and 100% drug coverage under PharmaCare Plan C.

aboutList.lead: Disability assistance is BC's core income program for people with the PWD designation.
items: A single person receives a $983.50 monthly support allowance plus a shelter allowance of up to $500 (for one person the minimum is $75 if your actual shelter costs are less), and every PWD recipient gets a $52 transportation supplement as cash or an in-kind bus pass.
It also opens the door to dental, optical, medical equipment, medical transportation and nutrition supplements, and 100% drug coverage under PharmaCare Plan C.

steps: Create an account at myselfserve.gov.bc.ca (or call 1-866-866-0800) and complete the online application so the ministry can check financial eligibility
Request the PWD designation application and complete the applicant section (form HR2883)
Have your doctor or nurse practitioner complete the medical report section
Have a doctor, nurse practitioner or prescribed professional (e.g., occupational therapist, social worker) complete the assessor report

Submit everything and respond to any ministry follow-up. If you are approved for the designation and are financially eligible, assistance is paid in the month following designation (payments begin in the month of your 18th birthday if you were designated before turning 18).
Report income and changes monthly as required to keep payments accurate
documents: ID and Social Insurance Number for all adults in the family unit
Bank statements and details of assets and income
Rent receipt, lease or proof of shelter costs
Completed PWD application (applicant, medical and assessor sections)
tips: Already on CPP Disability, Community Living BC, the At Home Program, PharmaCare Plan P (palliative) or ISC PWD? A simplified prescribed-class application (HR3642) skips most of the medical paperwork
You can take the $52 transportation supplement as a BC Bus Pass instead of cash. Choose whichever you actually use.
PWD has higher asset limits than regular income assistance, so savings do not disqualify you as quickly
At 65 most recipients move to federal Old Age Security and GIS. The ministry will contact you before then.
The earnings exemption runs January 1 to December 31 and does not carry over. Anything you do not use is gone, and you get a fresh limit each year.
There is no monthly limit. You can earn the whole exemption in one busy month or spread it across the year without your assistance changing.
Going over the limit does not cost you your earnings. Your assistance is reduced by the amount you went over, and you keep 100% of what you earned.
The ministry sends you a letter once you reach 75% of your exemption, and you can check what is left any time on My Self Serve.
If you start disability assistance partway through the year, your exemption is prorated for the months left in the year. A change in your family also changes your limit.
File monthly report HR0081 by the fifth of the month if you have income or any change to report. Report your income even when it is exactly the same as last month.
detail.time: Financial eligibility is usually confirmed within days; the PWD designation decision commonly takes several weeks to a few months once all three report sections are submitted

values.note: primary BC disability income support (support + max shelter + $52 transport); income-tested — excluded like AISH/ADAP
